finding.title: Fix curate_curricula/README.md status table: 13 of 14 curricula are marked TODO though main.py already implements them

evidence.quote: | **`mishneh_torah`** | Sefer / Hilchot / Perek / Halacha | NEW — TODO |

finding.why: README.md's Status column marks yerushalmi, mishnayos, chumash, nach, mishna_berurah, mussar, mishneh_torah, shulchan_arukh, arukh_hashulchan, kitzur_shulchan_aruch, chofetz_chaim and sefer_hamitzvot as TODO/'NEW — TODO', but main.py's STRATEGIES dict (lines 592-674) already has a complete, working strategy function for every one of them, plus shemirat_halashon which isn't in the table at all. A contributor or agent trusting this table would either re-implement already-finished strategies or believe the curation tool only covers Bavli.
finding.recommendation: Update the Status column to reflect main.py's STRATEGIES dict (mark implemented curricula done), add the missing shemirat_halashon row, and replace 'TODO' with the tool's actual remaining work (e.g. --diff review / spot-checking against Sefaria taxonomy).
acceptance_criteria: README.md Status column matches every key present in main.py's STRATEGIES dict
No curriculum with a working strategy function is labeled TODO

finding.title: Split or externalize tool/lib/sequences/halakhah_yomit_seq.dart — 1619-line hand-written Dart file violates the AG-3 400-line cap 4x over
finding.why: The file is 1619 lines of hand-typed string literals with no generated-file marker (not .g.dart/.freezed.dart), so AG-3's exemption doesn't apply; it is the single largest AG-3 violator in this batch by a wide margin (next largest tool/ file is 310 lines). The eventual `find lib test tool -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` checker described in coding-standards.md would flag it immediately.
finding.recommendation: Move the literal sequence to a tool/data/*.json asset loaded at seed-build time (the pattern already used for hebcal/sefaria calendar caches), or add an explicit '// GENERATED from Sefaria-Data — regenerate with <script>' header plus a regeneration script so it reads as generated output.
acceptance_criteria: File is <=400 lines or carries a recognized generated-file marker/extension
tool/seed_content_db.dart's halakhahYomitSequence lookup still resolves the same values after the change

finding.title: Extract the Sefaria TOC category-walk loop shared by curate_curricula/main.py (2x) and audit_seed.py (1x) instead of copy-pasting it

evidence.quote:
def _toc_subtree(path: str):
    """Walk Sefaria TOC categories by '/' delimited path, return the node."""
def _toc_books(category_path: str, main_subcats: list[str] | None = None):

finding.why: The same ~10-line 'split path on / and descend library.get_toc() matching category nodes' loop (identical toc/parts/node/contents/match variable names) is copy-pasted three times — twice inside main.py itself (_toc_subtree and _toc_books duplicate each other) and once more in audit_seed.py. A change to how Sefaria's TOC node shape is walked (e.g. a new category key) has to be found and patched in three places, and nothing keeps them in sync if only one gets fixed.
finding.recommendation: Extract a shared `_walk_toc_path(path) -> node | None` helper (e.g. a small tool/sefaria_toc_utils.py importable by both scripts) and have _toc_subtree, _toc_books, and _books_in_category call it.
acceptance_criteria: Only one implementation of the TOC-path-walk loop exists across tool/curate_curricula/main.py and tool/audit_seed.py
Sample category path (e.g. Talmud/Bavli/Seder Zeraim) resolves identically before/after the refactor

finding.title: Hoist duplicated seder-Hebrew-name and Torah-title static tables from sibling *_fetcher.dart classes into SefariaFetcherBase
finding.why: bavli_fetcher.dart and mishna_fetcher.dart each carry their own byte-identical 6-entry seder-name Hebrew map; chumash_fetcher.dart and nach_fetcher.dart each carry their own identical 5-book Torah-title list. All four subclasses extend SefariaFetcherBase, which is the natural single home for this static reference data, but it exposes neither — so a spelling fix or a new entry has to be applied in two files with nothing enforcing they stay in sync.
finding.recommendation: Add a shared `torahTitles` list and a `sederHebrewName(String)` lookup to SefariaFetcherBase (or a small shared sefaria_reference_data.dart) and have the four fetchers reference it instead of their private copies.
acceptance_criteria: Only one definition each of the seder-name map and the Torah-title list exists under tool/lib/sefaria/
bavli/mishna/chumash/nach fetcher output is unchanged after switching to the shared constant

finding.title: make audit's Rule 3/4 Firebase/Talker-confinement greps scan lib/ only, so tool/lib/dio_client.dart's raw Talker import is invisible to every gate
finding.why: Rule 4 says raw Talker import is confined to core/logging/; tool/lib/dio_client.dart imports it directly to build a Talker-backed Dio logger. tool/lib/ is part of the same Dart package (it imports package:learning_tracker/core/... elsewhere in this batch), but the audit's Rule 1-4 checks are hardcoded `grep ... lib/ --include="*.dart"` and custom_lint (the other enforcement path) is currently crashing entirely per the baseline — so nothing today, and nothing that will resume working once custom_lint is fixed unless its scope is also checked, would ever catch a Firebase- or Talker-misuse regression introduced under tool/.
finding.recommendation: Either extend the Rule 3/4 audit greps to also scan tool/lib/ (carving out this file with a stated justification — it's a dev-only CLI logger with no PII/Crashlytics surface), or add an explicit documented exemption for tool/ in coding-standards.md so the gap is a decision instead of a blind spot.
acceptance_criteria: coding-standards.md states whether tool/ is in scope for Rules 3/4
If in scope, make audit checks 2 and 4 cover tool/lib/ and dio_client.dart either routes through AppLogger or is added to a justified, named exemption
